verses.text: When Mordecai found out everything that had been done, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and covered himself with ashes. He went out into the city, crying loudly and bitterly.
He went only as far as the king's gate, because no one dressed in sackcloth was allowed to go through it.
In every province where the king's order arrived, the Jews mourned greatly. They went without food, cried, and wailed. Many of them lay on sackcloth and ashes.
Esther's servant girls and officials came and told her about Mordecai. The queen was very upset. She sent clothes for Mordecai to wear instead of his sackcloth, but he would not take them.
Then Esther called Hathach, one of the king's officials whom the king had chosen to serve her. She told him to go to Mordecai and find out what was wrong and why.
So Hathach went out to Mordecai in the city square in front of the king's gate.
Mordecai told him everything that had happened. He told him the exact amount of money Haman had promised to pay into the king's treasury for killing the Jews.

He also gave him a copy of the order to destroy the Jews, which had been announced in Susa, to show to Esther and explain to her. He told Hathach to urge her to go to the king, to beg him for mercy, and to plead with him for her people.
Hathach went back and told Esther what Mordecai had said.
Then Esther told Hathach to give Mordecai this message:

"All the king's officials and the people of the king's provinces know this law: anyone, man or woman, who goes to the king in the inner courtyard without being called must be put to death. The only exception is if the king holds out his gold scepter to that person. Then their life is spared. And I have not been called to go to the king for thirty days."
They told Mordecai what Esther had said.
Then Mordecai sent back this answer to Esther: "Do not think that because you are in the king's palace, you will escape when all the other Jews are killed.

If you keep quiet at a time like this, help and rescue for the Jews will come from somewhere else, but you and your father's family will die. Who knows? Maybe you became queen for a time just like this."
Then Esther sent this answer to Mordecai:

"Go and gather all the Jews in Susa. Go without food for me. Do not eat or drink anything for three days, night or day. My servant girls and I will also go without food. Then I will go to the king, even though it is against the law. And if I die, I die."
So Mordecai went away and did everything Esther had told him.
